title: Pattern matching
sub: is, switch expressions and arm order
cards/0/title: Check and extract in one go
cards/0/body: is checks the type and declares a variable at the same time. Property patterns look inside the object.
cards/0/code:
if (shape is Circle { R: > 10 } big)
    Console.WriteLine($"big circle {big.R}");
cards/1/body: Arms are checked top to bottom, and the first match wins. _ means "everything else", null included. The compiler complains (CS8510) if an arm can never be reached because everything is already caught above it.
cards/2/task: The arms are mixed up: a point becomes a circle, a square becomes a rectangle, and null becomes "something else". Put them in order with the ▲ buttons.
cards/3/q: Why did null end up in "something else"?
cards/3/options/0: _ catches everything, null included, and the null arm was below it
cards/3/options/1: You can't check for null in a switch
cards/3/explain: Specific cases go higher, general ones lower.
cards/5/explain: 95 is neither below 0 nor above 100, but it is ≥ 90 — the first matching arm.
cards/6/q: Not null and not an empty string
cards/6/explain: name is not null and not "" — it reads almost like plain English.
cards/7/q: Match the pattern to its meaning
cards/8/q: The arm Rect r sits above Rect { W: var w, H: var h } when w == h. What does the compiler say?
cards/8/options/0: CS8510: the second arm is unreachable — every Rect is already caught
cards/8/options/2: It picks the more specific arm by itself
cards/8/explain: The compiler doesn't reorder arms — the first one wins.
